sample_unit: imaging decisions rated (10 ACR breast imaging clinical variants)

links.outcome: Consistency and reproducibility of ChatGPT ratings across four independent samplings
links.effect: Current ChatGPT versions lack consistency and reproducibility relative to radiologists; radiologists were often as variable or less variable as a group than the same ChatGPT version.
links.quote: In summary, radiologists were closer to the ACR AC and were oftentimes as variable or even less variable as a group than the same ChatGPT version at the same time.

links.outcome: Agreement of ChatGPT imaging appropriateness ratings with ACR Appropriateness Criteria
links.effect: All ChatGPT versions had significant mean bias vs ACR (GPT-4o 2.463; GPT-4 1.7623; GPT-3.5 2.4691; all p<0.001) versus radiologists 0.2438 (p=0.489).
links.quote: All versions of ChatGPT had larger mean biases that were significant (GPT-4o: 2.463; GPT-4: 1.7623, GPT-3.5: 2.4691, all p<0.001).

links.outcome: ChatGPT versions versus breast radiologists agreement with ACR criteria
links.effect: Radiologists had lowest mean bias (0.2438, p=0.489) and smallest slope bias; all ChatGPT versions had significant bias (p<0.001).
links.quote: Radiologists had the lowest overall mean bias (0.2438) relative to the ACR (p = 0.489).

screen.reason: Compares ChatGPT outputs to breast radiologists on ACR Appropriateness Criteria clinical vignettes without testing a specific implementation safeguard or deployment practice.
